Grace / team — initial inventory below (summary first, full matrix attached):

Summary (as of 2026-05-22):
- Embeddings: Redwood-hosted embedding service; no external subprocessor (processed on dedicated pods for customers opting in).
- Logging/observability: third-party vendor LogTrak Inc. — processes aggregated logs; PII redaction in place, some metadata retained for debugging; EU traffic flows to us-east-1 for analysis.
- Analytics: internal analytics infra + partner Statsflow — only pseudonymized event-level data; PSD classification: low-risk.
- Ops/backups: S3-compatible backup provider (third-party) used for Dedicated customers in certain regions — handles encrypted backups.

See attached "subprocessor_matrix.xlsx" (tabbed by product area) for status columns: processes_PII (yes/no), hosts_EU_data (yes/no), signed_addendum (yes/no), contact.

Notes:
- We mark LogTrak Inc. as processing derived metadata that could include PII in edge cases; they have a signed DPA but Per-Account addendum is not used by all customers — we can offer to push an addendum for HealthCI.
- For Dedicated and Private customers we can restrict cross-border movement per region; for Hosted API customers we rely on regional routing and SCCs for transfers.

Attaching: subprocessor_matrix.xlsx

Marcus Lin
Director, Infrastructure Partnerships — Redwood Inference

Quick update on transfer mechanism and diagram:

- Transfer mechanism: For hosted customers we rely on updated EU-US SCCs executed in our DPA (2024 SCCs template + standard annex). Redwood signs as processor to customer controller; where a downstream subprocessor is used we maintain processor-to-processor/processor-to-subprocessor mapping in the DPA addendum. We can confirm that SCCs are in place for transfers as of our last contract refresh (2025-11).

- KMS custody: Our KMS is customer-key-capable for Dedicated/Private deployments; for Hosted we manage envelope keys but KMS zones are in us-west-2 and eu-west-1. Laura, can you add a short attestation?

- Data flow diagram: created a redacted schematic and uploaded to a shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyZ-example-dataflow-evidence (view-only). Diagram shows: client -> ingestion (EU region) -> preprocessing -> model serving (may cross to US for some model variants) -> storage/backup (encrypted) -> analytics (third-party). Key custody annotated next to storage; arrows indicate where SCCs apply.

Flag: HealthCI uses an EU controller; if they require strict in-region processing we can propose Dedicated capacity or VPC deployment (note pricing/lead time).

Neha Kapoor
Privacy Counsel — Redwood Inference

Hi Sarah — thanks for the patience. Attached are the requested artifacts and a short summary below. If you need anything redacted differently or a formal attestation on Redwood letterhead, tell me and I will route to Legal.

What we provided (attachments + links):
- subprocessor_matrix.xlsx (attached) — current inventory, which subprocessors touch PII, EU-hosting flags, and whether a signed addendum exists.
- data_flow_diagram_v2.pdf (attached) — redacted high-level diagram showing PII ingress in EU region, optional model variant routing to US, encrypted backups, and points where SCCs apply.
- Drive link with additional notes: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1XyZ-example-dataflow-evidence

Short answers to your checklist:
1) Subprocessors: See matrix; key subprocessors that may touch PII are LogTrak Inc. (observability) and S3BackupCo (backups for Dedicated regions). We can initiate a per-account addendum for LogTrak if HealthCI requires it.
2) Data flow: Diagram attached; EU data enters our ingestion clusters in eu-west-1. Depending on model variant choices (some larger model variants run in us-east), inference requests may route cross-border — this is controllable for Dedicated/Private deployments.
3) Transfer mechanism: EU-US transfers are governed by the SCCs in our DPA; Redwood signs as processor to controller, and we maintain a processor/subprocessor mapping in the DPA addendum.
4) KMS attestation: Laura has provided a short attestation (internal doc) indicating KMS zones and that customer-key options exist for Dedicated/Private. If you need a formal attestation letter, we can produce one within 3 business days.

Next steps: let us know if HealthCI wants a per-subprocessor addendum for LogTrak or a Dedicated capacity proposal to keep all processing in-region. Happy to jump on a 30-minute call to walk through the diagram.

Best,
